podcast.title: Collaboration with Earth Wind & Fire
podcast.body: Phil Collins, who had routinely incorporated Earth Wind & Fire's horn section into his tracks for years, finally returned the favor by teaming up with EWF singer Philip Bailey for the duet "Easy Lover." This collaboration resulted in a massive crossover hit in 1984, highlighting a long-standing musical connection. "Phil Collins, who'd been adding Earth Wind and Fire's horn section to his tracks for years. He finally returned the favor by teaming up with EWF singer Philip Bailey."

podcast.title: Influence on 1980s Snare Drum Sound
podcast.body: Phil Collins' distinctive drum sound profoundly influenced recording producers and engineers in the 1980s, marking a significant departure from earlier close-miking techniques. His sound, characterized as big, fat, boomy, and powerful, inspired the adoption of recording acoustic drums in large rooms with hard surfaces to incorporate natural echo and long decay, rather than seeking dead quiet environments. "The biggest influence on the new 80s snare drum sound was Phil Collins."

podcast.title: Ongoing Mobility Issues
podcast.body: Phil Collins's health challenges have continued for years, requiring treatment in a hyperbaric chamber for an infected diabetic abscess on his foot. He frequently relies on a cane for support and occasionally uses a wheelchair due to persistent problems with his back and hips. During the very last Genesis tour, he performed all his sets sitting down, with his son Nic taking over drumming duties. "He needs a cane and sometimes resorts to a wheelchair because of continuing problems with his back and hips."

podcast.title: Spinal Injury and Nerve Damage
podcast.body: In 2009, Phil Collins sustained a severe injury during a gig, dislocating a vertebrae in the upper part of his neck. This incident led to significant nerve damage that profoundly affected the function of his hands, making it difficult for him to hold drumsticks without taping them to his hands, and precluding him from playing the piano. "Everything started in 2009 during a gig when he injured a vertebrae in the upper part of his neck, a dislocation of some kind."

podcast.body: Phil Collins suffers from issues with his spine and immune system that severely impede his ability to walk. Consequently, when he performs live now, he is required to sing while sitting down. xref.title: Peter Gabriel Left 1975; Phil Collins Replaced Him After 40 Auditions; Ray Wilson Later Filled In
xref.body: Peter Gabriel was Genesis's founding singer from 1967 until his departure in 1975, which nearly ended the band. After approximately 40 auditions, they chose their own drummer Phil Collins, whose tenure extended the band's commercial reach considerably. In 1996–2000, when Collins was occupied with his solo career, a singer named Ray Wilson fronted the band before Collins returned. "You know, that worked out okay, didn't it?"

xref.body: Julian is the son of John Casablancas, founder of the Elite Model Management Agency, which managed stars like Cindy Crawford, Stephanie Seymour, Gisele Bündchen, Linda Evangelista, Naomi Campbell, Kendall Jenner, Pauline Apport's Gova, Claudia Schiffer, and Heidi Klum. His mother, a former Miss Denmark, encouraged his interest in bands like The Doors, moving him away from Phil Collins records. Julian had a teenage drinking problem, leading him to rehab in high school, which he attributed to his environment, rebelling to be closer to his father. The connection to the modeling agency proved useful, as models from Elite would attend early Strokes gigs, helping with attendance.
